why: On SpaceX's Oct 20 Q3 call, Musk said the Tesla and SpaceX boards have each formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a merger. He called it a good idea but said no terms are agreed and there's no guarantee (CNBC, BBC, WSJ, FT).

Nothing new overnight: SpaceX's 8-K is its earnings release with no Tesla merger language, and the overnight stories recap the committee news. The headline is 17.7% for a merger letter by Dec 31, 2026 and 58.0% by Jun 30, 2027, down slightly on time and a small dip in Kalshi and Polymarket prices. Wednesday's coverage (NYT, CNBC, Bloomberg, Fox Business) recaps the same news; Reuters adds, citing a person familiar, that Tesla is working with an investment bank and the deal could take the form of SpaceX acquiring Tesla. That fits the committee signal already counted, so no change.
The Dec 3 meeting is still routine, so a deal goes through a separate announcement, an S-4 and a 2027 special meeting. Tesla needs 50% of all outstanding shares, which Musk called a high hurdle.

Tesla's Q3 results came out Oct 21 with no merger language in the 8-K or shareholder deck, and on the call Musk said only that he'd said everything that should be said the day before. Evening coverage (WSJ, NYT, FT, Yahoo Finance) recaps the committee news, so no change. SpaceX's 1.3B-share unlock is Thursday Oct 22.

Oct 22: Reuters (a person with direct knowledge) says Musk's public endorsement rattled insiders and could delay the process by several weeks; talks are early, advisers are hired, and structures include SpaceX buying Tesla or a new holding company. Bloomberg (people familiar) says an announcement is targeted for the first half of 2027. Neither changes whether a deal happens, but both push it later, so the rules model moved weight from late 2026 into early 2027. Dec 31, 2026 odds fell from 18.0% to 13.4%; Jun 30, 2027 is about unchanged at 55.9%. Kalshi's May 1, 2027 contract dropped from 64.5% to 48% overnight on a thin quote.
